K. Air Quality: Little change in air quality is anticipated because of this action. With regard to vehicle emissions, EPA will be enforcing an emission standard for nonpassenger automobiles in MY 1979. The best engineering approach will require optimization of the vehicle design to meet both the emission standard and the AFES simultaneously. Therefore, the AFES is not likely to provide additional improvement in air quality when the manufacturer will already be optimizing his design to meet the EPA standard.
Two possible instances may exist where the AFES could conceivably affect individual vehicle emission levels. The first possibility is that a manufacturer may reduce his margin of safety by which he determines he must design his vehicles to exceed an applicable emission standard, in order to meet a fuel economy standard. Although the increase in emissions could be sufficiently small that the manufacturer would still be able to pass the EPA emission test and obtain certification, the safety margin to pass the test would be reduced and, theoretically, the average emissions of the manufacturer's fleet would increase.
